newsitem.title: UK: C&W shares up as Merrill raises price target.
newsitem.headline: C&W shares up as Merrill raises price target.

text.p: Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc climbed on Wednesday after analysts at Merrill Lynch said they had increased their earnings forecasts for the stock and raised their price target to 600p from 560.
The shares were 10-1/2p firmer at 506-1/2p by 0930 GMT.
News that C&W had cut its stake in Sweden's NetCom Systems, resulting in a gain of 40 million stg in the current year, also helped the stock, dealers said.
Merrill Lynch analyst Simon Carrington said estimates for C&W's 1997 pre-tax profits had been raised to 1.304 billion stg from 1.276 billion, while the 1998 forecast had been raised to 1.498 billion.
He said forecasts for 1999 earnings had been increased by seven percent.

"The key point is that C&W may become a smaller telecoms company but it should end up with bigger partners and it should be more profitable as a result of everything that's going on," Carrington said. "I expect it will be part of a global alliance by the end of this year."
